quest.51301102B4D1DEF4.quest_desc: The smallest Smeltery has a 1×1×1 interior. Place one Seared Bricks underneath it, then Controller, Fuel Tank, Drain and another Seared Bricks around the empty cell. Corners and the floor perimeter are unnecessary.
Attach a Faucet to the Drain and place a Basin below it. Supply lava to the tank. This kit melts and casts storage blocks; add a Casting Table and casts separately when needed.
Open the working Smeltery Controller to satisfy the retained native formation check. Expand the rectangular floor and walls for more capacity.
The tasks check each material and quantity without consuming it. Hold the kit before placing it, then complete the separate formation or operation check where this quest has one.
quest.51301102B4D1DEF4.title: The Mighty Smeltery
quest.5130110E810676F3.quest_desc: Learning route: start with the three pickaxe parts and repairs, then learn melting and replace the head with a metal one. Leave large tools, rare alloys and a full set of modifiers for later.
If the casting quests are still greyed out, check the shared Industrial Chassis milestone in the Main Route chapter. Being able to craft a block and unlocking its quest are separate conditions.
Lesson: Getting started: pattern, part, tool.
Modern Foundry provides this pack's modular tools. Begin with three steps: Pattern → Part Builder → Modern Foundry Station. You do not need a smeltery for your first pickaxe.
Take 2 planks and 2 sticks. Arrange them diagonally in a 2×2 crafting square: plank / stick in the top row, stick / plank in the bottom row. This makes 6 Patterns.

A Pattern is a consumable template for the Part Builder, where you select the shape of the part you want to make. A Pick Head is a finished pickaxe head. A Pick Head Gold Cast is a separate mold for casting metal. These are three different items; you do not need to pour gold into your first workbench.

First make a Part Builder and a Modern Foundry Station using the neighbouring quests. Set aside 2 flint and 2 planks for your practice pickaxe; the Part Builder quest explains how to turn them into the three required parts.
Search JEI for @modernfoundry to find this workshop's items. The English names used in these lessons match the installed mod version.
quest.5130110E810676F3.title: Obtain 1 × Pattern
quest.513011188AFE6ECD.quest_desc: Lesson: Rose Gold: a binding with an extra slot, and the large anvil.

Rose Gold in this version uses 90 mB copper + 90 mB gold → 180 mB alloy at 550°C. In other words, 1 copper ingot and 1 gold ingot make 2 Rose Gold ingots. Melt them together in a Smeltery or combine the fluids in an Alloyer; the small Melter cannot alloy.

A useful first part is a Rose Gold Tool Binding. Cast it and replace the wooden binding in a Modern Foundry Station. This material's Enhanced trait adds an upgrade slot, while the pickaxe head can remain iron or use another working metal.

Do not choose a Rose Gold head just because its name sounds more expensive: its base mining tier is gold. It is useful for combining material traits, but it is not automatically a better head than iron.

The next major step is Modern Foundry's Anvil. One valid recipe uses 3 matching blocks of an accepted alloy across the top row, with 4 Seared Bricks blocks below them in the shape of a stand. Rose Gold blocks are accepted. You need alloy BLOCKS, not three ingots.

Right-click the anvil to open it. It has room for large four-part tools: Sledge Hammer, Excavator, Vein Hammer, Broad Axe and Cleaver. Their individual quests give the exact part lists. A three-part crossbow can already be assembled at the ordinary station.
quest.513011188AFE6ECD.title: Obtain 1 × Rose Gold Ingot
quest.5130112084562752.quest_desc: Lesson: Cleaver: a slower heavy strike and Severing.

The Cleaver is a large weapon with a strong but slower attack. It starts with Severing II, which adds a chance of special drops from eligible mobs. That chance follows the particular drop's rules; it does not guarantee a head from every enemy.

Required parts: 1 Broad Blade, 2 Tough Handles and 1 Large Plate. Right-click a Modern Foundry's Anvil, select Cleaver and place all four parts. An ordinary sword's Small Blade does not fit this recipe.

For a weapon, compare the finished result's damage and attack speed, not only the material's mining tier. Late-game Manyullyn has a higher base head attack stat than Hepatizon, but the other parts and traits also change the result.

If you choose Manyullyn, its alloy recipe uses 270 mB cobalt and 90 mB Molten Debris at 1200°C to produce 360 mB. Prepare Blazing Blood for heating. First press R to check the complete cost of the Broad Blade and Large Plate.
You can keep an ordinary Sword for familiar, faster fights and reserve the Cleaver for a particular drop. A Blaze Head, for example, can later be melted into Blazing Blood for hot alloys.
quest.5130112084562752.title: Obtain 1 × Cleaver
quest.5130112804C9926A.quest_desc: Lesson: Cobalt: the Nether and faster parts.
Cobalt is a material for your next Nether expedition. Prepare a diamond-tier tool for cobalt ore. You can reach that tier with an Amethyst Bronze head or the Diamond modifier on an assembled pickaxe.
One current simple route to an ingot is Raw Cobalt or Nether Cobalt Ore → Blast Furnace → Cobalt Ingot. For making parts, subsequently melt the ingot at 950°C; lava is hot enough.

Cast a cobalt head, handle or binding and replace the corresponding part at the station. The Lightweight trait makes the tool work faster; the base head has 800 durability, speed 6.5 and a diamond mining tier.
Choose what you want to improve: Cobalt adds speed while remaining a diamond-tier material. For a netherite mining tier, see Hepatizon, Queen's Slime, Cinderslime or the separate Netherite modifier.
Keep a supply of cobalt for Hepatizon, Queen's Slime and other alloys. First cast one part you need and check its effect on your tool, then scale up production.
quest.5130112804C9926A.title: Obtain 1 × Cobalt Ingot
quest.5130112A675315EA.quest_desc: Lesson: Begin casting by making Grout.
Grout is the raw material for Seared Brick. Combine 1 Clay Ball, 1 sand and 1 gravel to make 2 Grout. For a larger batch, use 1 clay block, 4 sand and 4 gravel to make 8.
Put Grout into an ordinary furnace with fuel. Each block produces 1 Seared Brick. Then open the neighbouring Seared Brick quest for the complete first-melter checklist.
Keep 1 Grout for Puny Smelting: combine it with an ordinary Book, hold the result and right-click to open it. It shows the Melter and the placement of casting blocks.

If the metallurgy tasks are greyed out, check the Industrial Chassis quest in the 00 · Main Route chapter. It is the shared requirement for unlocking this part of the questbook. You can view the recipes and prepare Grout and workshop components in advance.
quest.5130112A675315EA.title: Obtain 1 × Grout
quest.5130112B7E67B5BF.quest_desc: Minimum Foundry: a solid 3×3 floor and a one-block-high 3×3 wall ring with an empty centre. Corners are required: its 17 shell positions are 14 Scorched Bricks, a Controller, a Fuel Tank and a Drain.
Attach a Scorched Faucet and Basin for casting, fuel the tank and open the controller. The native working-Foundry check remains mandatory.
The Foundry separates by-products and does not automatically alloy its fluids. Use a Smeltery or separate Alloyer for mixing.
The tasks check each material and quantity without consuming it. Hold the kit before placing it, then complete the separate formation or operation check where this quest has one.
quest.5130112B7E67B5BF.title: The Fantastic Foundry
quest.5130112F60A7AD22.quest_desc: Lesson: Slimesteel: durability and an Overslime reserve.
Alloy Slimesteel at 900°C: 90 mB iron + 250 mB Sky Slime + 250 mB Seared Stone → 180 mB Slimesteel. Use a lava-fuelled Smeltery or an Alloyer, and check that the recipe uses the correct slime type.

Sky Slime specifically means the sky variety. Do not substitute an ordinary green vanilla slime ball without checking. The floating slime island quest explains where to look; JEI shows valid raw materials for the required fluid.

Cast a Pick Head or the working part of a large tool. A Slimesteel head has base stats of 1040 durability, speed 6 and a diamond mining tier. It is an option for longer expeditions, not a required replacement for a faster head on every pickaxe.

The material supplies Overslime and Overcast. Overslime is a separate reserve consumed before ordinary durability; replenish it with suitable slime using modifier recipes. Overcast increases that reserve's capacity.

Put the assembled tool in the station and inspect its Overslime before travelling. Having a Slimesteel part does not mean infinite repairs. Ordinary repairs using the working part's material or a Repair Kit remain necessary too.
quest.5130112F60A7AD22.title: Obtain 1 × Slimesteel Ingot
quest.513011312C231A50.quest_desc: Lesson: Liquid fuel: lava and Blazing Blood.
Craft a Seared Fuel Tank from 8 Seared Brick around 1 glass block. Fill it with a lava bucket. Place it directly beneath a Melter; in a Smeltery, it belongs in a wall rather than the floor.

The fuel tank and the molten-metal reservoir serve different purposes. Put heating lava into the fuel tank. Put iron for a part into the Melter or Smeltery's item-input slots, then pour the molten metal out through a faucet.
Temperatures in this pack: Heater solid fuel — 800°C; lava — 1000°C; Blazing Blood — 1500°C. If a recipe needs 1050–1400°C, adding more buckets of lava will not raise its temperature above 1000°C.

Obtain Blazing Blood by melting Blazes inside a working Smeltery or Foundry. Another confirmed route is melting a Blaze Head at 1000°C; one head produces 100 mB. Severing can cause heads to drop, but a head is not guaranteed from every Blaze.
Transfer the finished hot fuel into the fuel tank before alloying Cinderslime, Queen's Slime or Hepatizon. Their quests give the exact temperatures and ingredients.
quest.513011312C231A50.title: Obtain 1 × Seared Fuel Tank
quest.5130113698719B61.quest_desc: Lesson: Ordinary crafting and repairs on the road.

The Modern Foundry Crafting Station handles ordinary recipes in a 3×3 grid. Its simple recipe is a Pattern above a log. Use the neighbouring Modern Foundry Station to assemble a pickaxe from parts; use this block for Patterns, workshop components and regular crafting.

Make a Repair Kit before setting out. For a flint pickaxe, select Repair Kit in the Part Builder and spend 2 flint. A kit has its own material too. Metal kits are cast using the appropriate mold, like other parts.

While travelling, open your inventory with E and put the damaged tool and a matching Repair Kit together in the 2×2 crafting grid. Take the repaired tool. The same repair works in a Crafting Station, so you do not need to return to the foundry for every scratch.

Match the Repair Kit's material to the tool's working part. On a simple pickaxe, that is the head. Once you install an iron Pick Head, the flint kit from your starting pickaxe is no longer the right spare.
Check your particular Repair Kit's material in its tooltip: two identical icons can contain different materials.
quest.5130113698719B61.title: Obtain 1 × Crafting Station
quest.51301143EEA55D59.quest_desc: Lesson: Heater: your first fuel and its temperature limit.

Craft a Seared Heater from a ring of 8 Seared Brick. Place it as the lower block with a Seared Melter directly above it. Use the melter interface to put coal or another valid furnace fuel into the fuel slot.
Solid fuel in this Heater supplies a temperature of 800°C. That is enough for your first iron casting, but not for every metal or alloy.
When you need more heat, replace the lower Heater with a Seared Fuel Tank and fill it with lava, which supplies 1000°C. You can leave the Melter, Faucet and table in place.
The Heater serves the small machine. Build the large Smeltery with its own fuel tank in a wall; placing this Heater underneath it does not replace the required structure.
quest.51301143EEA55D59.title: Obtain 1 × Seared Heater
quest.5130114557E8D53C.quest_desc: Lesson: Sort parts by shape and material.
Use a Part Chest for spare heads, handles, bindings and repair kits. Its recipe uses 1 wooden chest, 1 Pattern, 4 sticks and 1 plank.

Keep Pick Heads, Tool Handles, Tool Bindings and Repair Kits in separate groups. Within each group, arrange materials together: flint for starting out, iron for your first cast parts and your chosen alloy for the next replacement.

Hover over every part before assembling a tool. The head sets a pickaxe's base mining tier, the handle changes its stats and the binding can supply a material trait. You do not have to put the most expensive metal into all three slots.
Keep one inexpensive sample head for making a cast, and store your working pickaxe's repair materials separately. Making a gold cast consumes the sample; you do not need to sacrifice a finished tool.
quest.5130114557E8D53C.title: Obtain 1 × Part Chest
quest.5130114A1BBCC155.quest_desc: Lesson: Excavator: dirt, sand and gravel in a 3×3 area.
The Excavator digs dirt, sand, gravel and similar shovel-type blocks in a 3×3 area. For a stone tunnel, use the Sledge Hammer, which is a different tool.
Take 1 Large Plate, 2 Tough Handles and 1 Tough Collar. Right-click a Modern Foundry's Anvil, select Excavator, put the four parts into the matching silhouettes and collect the result.
The working part here is the Large Plate, so choose its material for durability and speed. The handles can use a different material if it supplies the stats you want.

The ordinary three-slot Modern Foundry Station cannot fit this set. If the assembly option is unavailable, check which station block you are using. You need the large anvil whose recipe is explained in the Rose Gold quest.
Before starting a quarry, prepare repair supplies for the working plate's material and storage space for many blocks. Test the tool on a small area to see the orientation of its digging pattern.
quest.5130114A1BBCC155.title: Obtain 1 × Excavator
quest.5130114E49A3B3A2.quest_desc: Find a Modern Foundry sky slime island and enter its structure. The quest checks for Sky Slime Island, not merely a high-altitude biome or any green slime ball in your inventory.
Your workshop needs a source of Sky Slime for Slimesteel. Process the Sky Slime you collect into the corresponding fluid using the JEI recipe.
Alloy reminder: 90 mB iron + 250 mB Sky Slime + 250 mB Seared Stone → 180 mB Slimesteel at 900°C. A lava-fuelled Smeltery can do this.

This is an optional expedition. You do not need to grow resource crops for it, and the island is not required for your first pickaxe or iron casting. Before climbing, bring building blocks, a way to descend safely and a Repair Kit.
quest.5130114E49A3B3A2.title: Skyslime Island
quest.513011509432E58F.quest_desc: Lesson: Amethyst Bronze: a diamond-tier head.

Amethyst Bronze is a useful next head material. Its alloy recipe is 90 mB copper + 100 mB molten amethyst → 90 mB bronze at 820°C. Lava at 1000°C works; the Heater's 800°C solid fuel is no longer hot enough.

Prepare 180 mB of bronze for a Pick Head: two batches of this recipe. Select the alloy in the Smeltery, pour it into a Pick Head Gold Cast on a Casting Table and collect the cooled head. Use it to replace the iron head in a Modern Foundry Station.

This material's base head stats are 720 durability, mining speed 7 and a diamond mining tier. These are the head's values before other parts and modifiers are applied, not guaranteed final stats for every pickaxe.

This head supports the transition from iron to obsidian and the next stage of metallurgy. Its Crumbling trait also speeds up breaking blocks that do not require a tool. For an ordinary pickaxe, you can keep a wooden handle and a Rose Gold binding.

Make a matching Repair Kit and reserve some bronze for repairs. Then choose a direction: Slimesteel for durability and Overslime, or Cobalt/Hepatizon for speed. You do not need to replace every part with the same alloy.
quest.513011509432E58F.title: Obtain 1 × Amethyst Bronze Ingot
quest.51301173518ABE85.quest_desc: Lesson: Sledge Hammer: a 3×3 stone tunnel.
The Sledge Hammer is a large mining tool for stone and ore in a 3×3 area. It is a useful next step after an ordinary pickaxe when you want to cut corridors or clear rooms.
Required parts: 1 Hammer Head, 1 Tough Handle and 2 Large Plates. Open a Modern Foundry's Anvil, select Sledge Hammer and place all four parts into the matching silhouettes.

The Hammer Head's material sets the tool's main characteristics, and both plates also affect its stats. For your first hammer, use casting materials you already produce reliably; the parts do not all have to be the same metal.
Do not confuse it with the Vein Hammer. The Sledge Hammer cuts a 3×3 plane, while the Vein Hammer follows neighbouring blocks of the same type. Choose for the job, not whichever icon looks heavier.

Check the finished hammer's mining tier and prepare a Repair Kit it accepts. Before a long tunnel, try it on ordinary stone: a large tool uses up its reserves while working, rather than merely taking up a hotbar slot.
quest.51301173518ABE85.title: Obtain 1 × Sledge Hammer
quest.5130117B8B2F0B26.quest_desc: The foundry will faithfully reproduce any shape. Even the one you placed by accident and now insist was intentional.
Lesson: Broad Axe: a tool for whole trees.
The Broad Axe is a large tree-felling tool. On a tree, it processes connected logs, making it useful for gathering wood; it is not another ordinary pickaxe.

This version's exact parts are 1 Broad Axe Head, 1 Tough Handle, 1 Pick Head and 1 Tough Collar. Yes, a pickaxe head is included. Select Broad Axe in a Modern Foundry's Anvil and follow the slot silhouettes rather than the finished axe's name.

Cast the working head from an available durable material, then choose the handle and additional parts for the traits you want. A material having a Pick Head recipe does not mean every other part type accepts exactly the same selection; check with R.
Test the axe on a separate tree first and prepare space for the wood. Large log-built structures are also unsuitable practice targets for your first strike.
This tool handles wood gathering. Keep an Excavator for dirt, and a pickaxe or Sledge Hammer for stone. One expensive item does not have to perform every job around your base.
quest.5130117B8B2F0B26.title: Obtain 1 × Broad Axe
quest.5130118269A1E560.quest_desc: Lesson: Faucet: where the metal should flow.

A Seared Faucet transfers fluid into the block directly below its spout. Attach it to the side of the Melter. Put a Casting Table or Casting Basin one block below the faucet itself, not beneath the centre of the melter.

On a large Smeltery, attach the faucet to a Seared Drain in the wall. The controller opens the interface, the fuel tank supplies heat and the Drain outputs metal: these blocks have three different jobs.
Place the required cast on the Casting Table, check your molten-metal supply and right-click the Faucet. Wait for pouring and cooling to finish, then right-click the table to collect the cast part.

If the Smeltery contains several fluids, click the one you want in its interface to select it for pouring. The Faucet cannot infer the metal from a quest's name. In a Melter, you must first empty the single tank completely of the previous fluid.

If nothing pours, check that the table is under the spout, the cast is correct, enough fluid is available and the output is clear. Your first iron head needs 180 mB of iron; 90 mB supplies only one material unit.
quest.5130118269A1E560.title: Obtain 1 × Seared Faucet
quest.5130118347056838.quest_desc: Minimum station: put one Melter above one Heater. Attach one Faucet to the Melter side and put one Casting Table below its spout. This layout occupies 2×2×1. The Heater burns solid fuel; a liquid-fuel tank can replace it later.
The kit is checked in inventory without consumption. Prepare fuel and a cast for the part separately; this item quest does not verify the melting process.
Lesson: Melter: one metal, three input slots.
The Seared Melter is a small starting machine. Place it directly on a solid-fuel Seared Heater or a liquid-fuel Seared Fuel Tank. Right-click the upper block to open it.

For your first iron head, put 2 iron ingots into the three upper input slots. Supply fuel below and wait for the ingots to melt. The metal will then flow through a Faucet into a Pick Head cast on a Casting Table.
The Melter can hold only ONE fluid type at a time. Drain the previous fluid completely before changing metals. If you melted gold for a cast first, do not add iron while gold still occupies the tank.

This machine cannot alloy different metals. Rose Gold and other alloys need a Smeltery or a separate Alloyer. Use the Melter for your first metal parts and the copper needed for a Smeltery Controller.

If melting stops, check the fuel directly below the Melter, drain any remaining previous metal and check the temperature required by the JEI recipe. Three item slots do not mean three separate fluid tanks.
quest.5130118347056838.title: Melter: First Melting Station Kit
quest.51301183F0DE5463.quest_desc: Lesson: Separate raw materials, casts and finished items.
Modern Foundry's Chest accepts ordinary items, so use it for Patterns, casting molds, ingots and books. Use the Part Chest beside it for finished Pick Heads, Handles, Bindings and Repair Kits.
Craft it with 1 wooden chest, 1 Pattern, 4 lapis lazuli and 1 plank. Press R over this task's icon to see the layout. Right-click the chest itself to open it.

Useful supplies for your first cast: iron ingots, 1 gold ingot for a reusable cast, an inexpensive sample head and fuel. The sand-cast alternative needs sand and a sample instead; the Casting Table quest explains both options.
First get one line working: melter → faucet → table. Extra chests make storage easier, but they do not move molten metal by themselves. You do not need to set up farming automation for this chapter.
quest.51301183F0DE5463.title: Obtain 1 × Modern Foundry's Chest
quest.513011885727A0B6.quest_desc: Smelting Grout produces Seared Brick, an individual brick item. Arrange 4 of these in a square to make the Seared Bricks building block. Different recipes need different forms, so press R over the exact icon.

For your first line, prepare a Seared Heater, Seared Melter, Seared Faucet and Seared Casting Table. Put the Heater at the bottom and the Melter directly on top. Attach the Faucet to the side of the Melter and place the casting table directly beneath the faucet's spout.

The Melter recipe also needs a glass Seared Fuel Gauge or Seared Ingot Gauge. Each of these gauges uses 4 Seared Brick and 5 glass blocks; the Melter itself adds another 5 bricks to the gauge. Ordinary glass cannot take the gauge's place without first being crafted into it.
Basic costs: Heater — 8 bricks; Casting Table — 7 bricks; 3 bricks make 3 Faucets at once. You will need a Seared Casting Basin a little later for the large smeltery's controller.
Keep the required items in your inventory long enough for their quests to detect them, then place them. These tasks consume nothing. The neighbouring quests explain how to use each block.
quest.513011885727A0B6.title: Obtain 1 × Seared Brick
quest.513011890D0653EB.quest_desc: Lesson: Cast an iron head in either of two ways.
Craft a Seared Casting Table from 7 Seared Brick and place it under a Faucet. It casts ingots and parts; use a Casting Basin for full blocks.

Method 1: a reusable gold cast. Make an inexpensive flint Pick Head in the Part Builder and right-click to place it on the table. Melt 1 gold ingot and pour 90 mB of gold over the sample. The sample is consumed, leaving a Pick Head Gold Cast on the table.
Drain any remaining gold completely from the Melter, melt 2 iron ingots and pour 180 mB of iron into the cast. Once it cools, take the iron Pick Head. The gold cast stays available for further parts.

Method 2: a single-use sand cast. Put a Blank Sand Cast on the table, click it with an inexpensive Pick Head to make the impression, then click again to retrieve the sample. Pour metal into the impression. Collecting the metal part consumes the sand cast, but this method needs no gold. Blank Sand Casts and shaped sand casts can also be made in the Part Builder; press R to inspect them.

Now put your pickaxe and the iron Pick Head into a Modern Foundry Station, check the replacement result and collect it. You can keep the wooden handle and binding. From now on, repair this pickaxe with iron or an iron Repair Kit.

Each other part needs its matching cast: a Small Blade Gold Cast cannot produce a Pick Head. Press R over the desired part to check its cast, metal quantity and valid materials; press U over an ingot to see its uses.
quest.513011890D0653EB.title: Obtain 1 × Seared Casting Table
quest.5130118F7AC78589.quest_desc: Lesson: Hepatizon: hot fuel and a fast head.
Hepatizon needs 1400°C. Prepare Blazing Blood in the fuel tank first: lava supplies only 1000°C and cannot start this alloy recipe even with a full tank.

The exact recipe is 180 mB copper + 90 mB cobalt + 100 mB molten quartz → 180 mB Hepatizon. This is the installed version's recipe; do not replace the quartz with obsidian based on another Tinkers pack.
One batch produces enough for a Pick Head. Pour 180 mB of alloy into the matching cast on a Casting Table, wait for it to cool and replace the head in a Modern Foundry Station.
The base head has 975 durability, speed 8 and a netherite mining tier. Momentum builds speed while you keep mining blocks or firing shots; the final stats depend on the entire tool.

For a mining pickaxe, this is a straightforward late-game direction: a stronger head, a useful handle and a binding with the trait you want. Also make a Repair Kit from the material now used to repair your tool.
quest.5130118F7AC78589.title: Obtain 1 × Hepatizon Ingot
quest.51301197819E7391.quest_desc: Lesson: Make the three parts of your first pickaxe.

Craft a Part Builder with 2 Patterns above 2 planks. Place it and right-click to open it. Put a Pattern in the pattern slot and flint or planks in the material slot, then choose the part using the buttons inside the interface.
First part: select Pick Head, insert 2 flint and take the flint head. A head costs 2 material units; one flint supplies one unit.

Second part: select Tool Handle, insert 1 plank and take the wooden handle. Third part: select Tool Binding, insert 1 more plank and take the wooden binding. Each of these two parts costs one material unit.

Your practice pickaxe needs 1 flint Pick Head + 1 wooden Tool Handle + 1 wooden Tool Binding. Refill the Patterns when they run out. The material determines the finished part's properties: the name Pick Head alone does not mean that it is an iron head.

Iron and the other cast metals in this version cannot be shaped in the Part Builder; cast metal parts on a Casting Table. For now, take your three finished parts to the Modern Foundry Station. Its quest explains assembly and your first repair.
quest.51301197819E7391.title: Obtain 1 × Part Builder
quest.5130119C5F8C1957.quest_desc: Lesson: Challenge: five bonuses on ONE tool.

This is a longer challenge involving extra slots. All five modifiers must be present AT THE SAME TIME on one tool: Writable, Recapitated, Harmonious, Forecast and Gilded. One extra slot, or five separate tools, does not meet the condition.
Writable: add a Book and Quill. Recapitated: add an accepted mob head; the dragon head is excluded from this recipe. Harmonious: add a music disc. Each of these modifiers unlocks 1 upgrade slot.
Forecast: add a whole diamond, emerald or cobalt ore block accepted by the JEI recipe. You need an ore block, not a diamond, emerald or Raw Cobalt. This also unlocks 1 upgrade slot.
Gilded: add Gilded Blackstone. It consumes 1 ability slot and supplies 2 upgrade slots. Keep an ability slot free on the tool you use for this challenge.

Apply them one after another in a Modern Foundry Station or Anvil, taking the tool from the result slot each time. These five bonuses together supply +6 upgrade slots and consume 1 ability slot. After the final addition, keep the finished tool in your inventory.
Do not delay your first working pickaxe for this challenge. You can start with Writable and find the required ore block and drops later.
quest.5130119C5F8C1957.title: All the Upgrades
quest.513011B07B76EA2C.quest_desc: Lesson: Cinderslime: turning fuel into Overslime.
Cinderslime is a hot slime alloy. Combine 90 mB gold, 250 mB Ichor and 250 mB Scorched Stone to obtain 180 mB of alloy at 1050°C. You need fuel hotter than lava, such as Blazing Blood.
Ichor, Sky Slime and ordinary green slime are different fluids. Scorched Stone is also different from Seared Stone. Press R to open the Cinderslime recipe and prepare the exact named ingredients.

Cast one part you need and install it on the tool. The base head has 1221 durability, speed 6.5 and a netherite mining tier, but this material's defining feature is the combination of Overslime and Overburn.

Overburn lets the tool convert liquid fuel into Overslime and adds fuel capacity inside the tool itself. This is a specialised option that makes sense once you already have a supply of the required liquid fuel.

If you want a straightforward working pickaxe without maintaining an internal fuel reserve, compare the finished result with Hepatizon or another familiar head. This quest introduces a choice of mechanics; it does not require converting every tool to Cinderslime.
quest.513011B07B76EA2C.title: Obtain 1 × Cinderslime Ingot
quest.513011B95D8BBC10.quest_desc: Lesson: Your first modifiers and their different slots.

Add a modifier to an already assembled tool in a Modern Foundry Station or Modern Foundry's Anvil. Select repair/modification mode, insert the tool and required ingredients, check the result and take it. The quest triggers when your inventory detects a tool with an added upgrade.

A simple starting point is a pickaxe plus 1 diamond. Diamond uses 1 upgrade slot, adds durability and speed, and sets the mining tier to diamond. This lets you progress beyond an iron head once you have a diamond to spare.

For mining speed, use Haste: 45 redstone or 5 redstone blocks provide one full level. Each level uses 1 upgrade slot, up to 5 levels. Supply the materials in the modification interface and take the result as needed.

An ordinary pickaxe starts with 3 upgrade slots and 1 ability slot. These are separate resources. Before filling the upgrade slots with assorted bonuses, decide whether you need a higher mining tier, more speed or room for Netherite later.

Replacing the head changes a material; adding a diamond or redstone changes modifiers. A tool plus a new part and a tool plus modifier ingredients are different recipes in the same station. Find their recipes in Modern Foundry's modifier category.
quest.513011B95D8BBC10.title: Modification
quest.513011BD6664E0BF.quest_desc: Lesson: Netherite mining tier: a head or a modifier.
The quest checks the modular tool's actual mining tier: Netherite. A netherite ingot in your inventory, or an expensive-sounding part name, does not meet the requirement.

Route 1 — material. Cast a Pick Head from Hepatizon, Queen's Slime or Cinderslime, replace the head on an ordinary modular pickaxe and take the result into your inventory. These heads specify a netherite mining tier in their material data.

Route 2 — the Netherite modifier. Put the assembled tool, 1 Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template and 1 Netherite Ingot into a Modern Foundry Station or Anvil. You need 1 free upgrade slot. This is a Modern Foundry modifier recipe.

Netherite improves the stats and sets the required tier. Inspect the finished tool's data in the station to understand its current properties; Cobalt or Amethyst Bronze's diamond tier alone is not netherite tier.

Check repairs before a long trip. The Netherite modifier does not replace the head material: if the head remains iron, ordinary repairs still need that material. If you instead replace the head with an alloy, prepare repair supplies made from that alloy.
quest.513011BD6664E0BF.title: Netherite Tier
quest.513011D18DBB23A0.quest_desc: You wanted one component. Now you have a production process, a separate building and a firm belief that this saves time.
Lesson: Assemble a pickaxe, then repair it.
Craft a Modern Foundry Station with 3 Patterns across the top row and 4 planks at the sides of the two lower rows. Place it and right-click. Select the Pickaxe icon from the tool list.

Put the flint Pick Head, wooden Tool Handle and wooden Tool Binding into the slots with the matching silhouettes. Take the finished pickaxe from the output slot. Separate heads and handles cannot mine; you need an assembled tool.

This is an inexpensive starting pickaxe with a stone mining tier. Your next step is to cast an iron Pick Head and replace only the head: put the finished pickaxe and the new head into this station's repair/modification mode, check the result and take the upgraded tool.

To repair at your base, put the damaged pickaxe into the station with its head material. A flint head needs flint; an iron head needs iron. A wooden handle does not let you repair an iron pickaxe with planks. When you replace the head, update your supply of repair materials too.

For your first Sword, this version requires 1 Small Blade + 2 Tool Handles. You can start with a flint blade and wooden handles. Select Sword in the station; do not put a pickaxe binding into the sword's third slot.
The basic station has three input slots. Large tools made from four parts are assembled on a Modern Foundry's Anvil. The Rose Gold Ingot quest explains its recipe and when to make the upgrade.
quest.513011D18DBB23A0.title: Obtain 1 × Modern Foundry Station
quest.513011D2087879F0.quest_desc: Lesson: Basin: the large smeltery's controller.
Craft a Seared Casting Basin from 7 Seared Brick. Put it beneath a Faucet in place of a table. It casts blocks and controllers.

Your first important recipe: put a Seared Bricks block into the Basin, melt 4 copper ingots and pour 360 mB of copper over it. After cooling, collect the Smeltery Controller. The brick block is consumed.
For ordinary metal blocks, the Basin requires the quantity shown in JEI. Avoid pouring your entire reserve of a rare metal into a block when you only need a small pickaxe head on a Casting Table.

Next, open the quest about forming a working Smeltery. Install the controller in a valid structure with a floor, walls, a fuel tank and a Drain. Simply holding the controller does not complete the task for opening the smeltery.
quest.513011D2087879F0.title: Obtain 1 × Seared Casting Basin
quest.513011D8F5E8633F.quest_desc: Lesson: Queen's Slime: trading durability for Overslime.

Alloy Queen's Slime at 1150°C: 90 mB cobalt + 90 mB gold + 250 mB Magma → 180 mB alloy. Use Blazing Blood for the temperature, and find the appropriate magma-material melting recipe in JEI to make Magma.
Cast a Pick Head or another required part, then replace it in a Modern Foundry Station or Anvil. The base head stats are 1650 durability, speed 6 and a netherite mining tier.

The material supplies Overslime and Overlord. Overlord converts some ordinary durability into Overslime capacity, so the material reference's value of 1650 is not the final ordinary durability of every assembled pickaxe.

Choose this direction if you want to maintain a large slime reserve. Compare the finished tool in the station: Overslime capacity, speed, ordinary durability and available slots. The largest number in one stat does not describe the whole tool.

If the netherite-tier quest has not completed yet, try installing this head on an ordinary modular pickaxe and take the result into your inventory. The dedicated tier quest explains the exact condition and the alternative Netherite-modifier route.
quest.513011D8F5E8633F.title: Obtain 1 × Queen's Slime Ingot
quest.513011D97B83053D.quest_desc: Lesson: Which book to read at each stage.
Combine an ordinary Book and a Pattern in any crafting slots to make Materials and You. Hold the book and right-click in the air to open it.

Start with the Part Builder and Modern Foundry Station sections, then read Pickaxe, Repairing and Part Swapping. They explain simple tools, repairs and replacement parts. If JEI displays an unusual translation, each lesson also includes the relevant English item name in parentheses.
For the small melter, make Puny Smelting from an ordinary Book and 1 Grout. It explains the Melter, faucets and casts. The opening pages of Materials and You do not cover all of metallurgy.

After the small melter, make Mighty Smelting: place an ordinary Book on a Casting Table and pour 250 mB of Seared Stone over it. This book includes a three-dimensional Smeltery diagram and large tools. Fantastic Foundry is made from an ordinary Book and Nether Grout; it explains the separate Scorched Foundry.
There is also the Encyclopedia of crafting for browsing modifiers: place an ordinary Book on a Casting Table and pour 90 mB of molten gold over it.
quest.513011D97B83053D.title: Obtain 1 × Materials and You
quest.513011EA4F627DEC.quest_desc: Lesson: Ender Slime: a later optional expedition.
Find a Modern Foundry Ender Slime island in the End and enter its structure. It must be an End Slime Island; an ordinary End island or an Ender Slime Ball in your inventory does not count as a visit.
Ender Slime is used in later materials, including Knightslime: 90 mB cobalt + 250 mB Ender Slime + 250 mB Molten Obsidian → 180 mB alloy at 1125°C. This temperature needs fuel hotter than lava.
Use item tooltips to distinguish slime types. Ender Slime cannot substitute for Sky Slime in Slimesteel or Ichor in Cinderslime.

This is an optional branch after reaching the End. You can learn the basic workshop, casting, large anvil and a working set of tools earlier. Bring finished tools and a Repair Kit, rather than only an impressive collection of plans.
quest.513011EA4F627DEC.title: Enderslime Island
quest.513011EB9F7495C4.quest_desc: Lesson: Crossbow: three parts and a supply of arrows.

The Modern Foundry Crossbow uses three parts: Bow Limb, Bow Grip and Bowstring. It is a compact tool that you can build at the basic Modern Foundry Station; a large anvil is not required for assembly itself.

For a simple start, use the Part Builder to make a Bow Limb from 2 planks, a Bow Grip from another 2 planks and a Bowstring from 4 string. Select each part in the workbench interface and refill Patterns as needed. Bow materials differ from the list for pickaxe heads; press R over the part to check valid options.

Right-click the Modern Foundry Station, select Crossbow and put the three parts into the matching silhouettes. Take the finished crossbow and keep arrows in your inventory. Hold the use-item control to load it; using it again after loading fires the shot.
When changing materials, inspect the Bow Limb and Bow Grip stats: draw speed, projectile velocity, accuracy and durability. A material that excels in a pickaxe may have an unfavourable draw speed.

Apply Modern Foundry modifier recipes for upgrades and check the station for free slots. The quest completes when the finished crossbow is in your inventory; it does not require one particular expensive configuration.
quest.513011EB9F7495C4.title: Obtain 1 × Crossbow
quest.513011F8FB529249.quest_desc: Lesson: Vein Hammer: follow a vein, not a plane.
The Vein Hammer mines neighbouring blocks of the same type within a vein. The Sledge Hammer makes a straight 3×3 tunnel; choose this hammer when you want to collect a connected ore deposit.
Take 1 Hammer Head, 1 Tough Handle, 1 Tough Collar and 1 Large Plate. Right-click a Modern Foundry's Anvil, select Vein Hammer and place the four parts using the slot guides.
Choose a working-head tier that can mine your intended ore. The head and plate can use different materials; compare the finished stats in the anvil's output preview.

This is the tool's own mechanic, so you do not need to enable FTB Ultimine. First test the hammer on a small visible vein. Ordinary stone is also one block type, so choose your first strike carefully.
The task checks for an assembled Vein Hammer in your inventory with any valid material configuration. A collection of its separate parts does not complete the quest.
quest.513011F8FB529249.title: Obtain 1 × Vein Hammer
